claim: Every declared instruction receives an explicit verdict from a fixed vocabulary — and an instruction with no mechanical checker is reported as unenforceable, never counted as satisfied.

steps.label: three instructions, two with checkers
steps.evidence: one row per declared instruction: 3 of 3
steps.note: The instructions nobody could check are exactly the ones worth knowing about. Leaving them out of the report is how a policy that verifies a third of itself reads as green.

steps.label: what the report says about coverage
steps.evidence: 'nothing failed' and 'everything was verified' are different statements

steps.label: not_applicable is not passed

request.INS-002: no module-level assignments exist to check

steps.note: An instruction with nothing to apply to has not been satisfied. Collapsing the two inflates every percentage in the report.

steps.label: a checker trying to mark its own instruction unenforceable
steps.note: Unenforceable is what the absence of a checker produces. If a checker could return it, an instruction could mark itself unverifiable and vanish from the part of the report anyone reads.

steps.label: a checker that invents a verdict
a checker that raises
steps.note: A broken checker invalidates the whole report rather than failing one instruction. A report that is wrong somewhere unknown is worse than no report.
